schema_note.purpose: The HUD of rounds 6 and 6b as data, for Latch to generate USS/UXML. Everything is px at the 1920x1080 reference unless a key says otherwise.

top_level.type_styles: name -> {font, weight, size_px, color (a colour variable), letter_spacing_px, line_height_px, uppercase}
top_level.colors: variable name -> hex and role; --<name> in USS
top_level.colors_delta_e: CIEDE2000 of each colour against the reserved signals (all >= 20)
top_level.reserved_signals: cone, guard and rival colours; only for small pictograms (signal_* sprites), never panel or text colours
top_level.sprites: name -> files at 1x and 2x, size, slice insets (left/top/right/bottom, px of that file) when nine-sliced, windows/content rects, margin
top_level.classes: state and kind class names with what each changes
top_level.docks: anchor rules for left_column, corner, bottom
top_level.pieces: one record per HUD piece: sprite, size, position (anchor/offset or relative_to), padding [top,right,bottom,left], children with rects relative to the piece (or to a window)

conventions: rect = [x, y, w, h] relative to the parent piece's top-left unless stated; 'auto' means size to text
sprite names refer to sprites; 'x|y' means one of
slice insets: use them as -unity-slice-left/top/right/bottom on the @1x file; for the @2x file use its own insets with -unity-slice-scale: 0.5px (or set the texture scale so 2 texels = 1 px)
states are USS classes on the element: .busy .ready .hurt .down .selected .disabled .hover .pressed .new .unread .live .folded .collapsed .compact .locked .armed .kind-*
acknowledge = K, history = L, cancel = Backspace (selected agent), hide hint = H, carry = C, verbs = 1-4, agents = F1-F4, show all strips = Tab

from: briefs/011/ui rounds 6 and 6b (finish r04 cab cluster, dock left column, compact default)

reference.textures: ship @2x with USS slice scale so 4K is sharp; @1x for 1080p-only builds
reference.min_text_note: reading text is 12 px and up; keycap, number-plate and tag labels (10.5-11.5 px, bold caps or numerals) are the exception
reference.note: at 1440p and 4K everything scales uniformly from the left, top-right and bottom-right anchors; characters stay 40-60 px (zoom limit), so the HUD does not change with zoom
